problems.prompt: For a circle, C = πd = 2πr. Explain why πd and 2πr give the same circumference.

fields.label: Explain
fields.answer: The diameter is twice the radius: d = 2r. Substituting 2r for d gives πd = π(2r) = 2πr.

solution: A diameter is made of two radii, so d = 2r.
problems.hint: A diameter passes all the way across the circle through its center.

problems.prompt: Compare the 6-, 12-, 24-, and 48-gons. What happens to r − h as the number of sides doubles? Explain why the height gets closer to the radius.

fields.label: Explain
fields.answer: The difference gets smaller and approaches zero. The triangles become narrower, so their perpendicular height gets closer to their radius-length sides.

solution: The gaps are about 0.8038, 0.2044, 0.0513, and 0.0128 cm. The narrowing triangles have heights approaching 6 cm.

notes: All finite regular polygon base lengths equal half the polygon perimeter.
Finite rearranged heights are apothems and approach the radius as the number of sides grows.
The exact 12-gon calculation uses a radial base and its perpendicular height, not a rounded apothem.
Partial-unit checks measure whole units plus cut halves.
Circumference concepts use nine-decimal given side lengths; perimeter is rounded to six decimals before calculating P/d.
